before: When a paragraph split left one letter between a dropped extra copy of an inline marker and the tail that moved away, the text diff treated the letter as part of a replacement and wrote it again as a new character. The new character had its own identity, so a peer's concurrent deletion of the letter did not hide it, and deleted text showed again.
after: The diff keeps a letter in place when no inserted text sits on either side of it, so the letter keeps its identity and a peer's deletion of it still applies.
reason: Only how a replica writes its own edit to existing shared text changes; it writes fewer new characters. Older clients read the result as before. Shared fields, operations, and synchronization keep their meaning.
